title: Finding supporting details
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: The main idea needs support. Supporting details are the smaller facts and examples that prove or explain the main idea. Quick words: supporting detail means small facts or examples that prove the main idea. main idea means the big point the writer wants you to know.
A supporting detail is a smaller fact or example that backs up the main idea.
Read this: 'The library is a helpful place. It has thousands of books, quiet reading corners, and kind helpers who find what you need.'

blocks.question: Which sentence is a supporting DETAIL, not the main idea?
options: The library is a helpful place.
blocks.explain: 'It has quiet reading corners' is a small fact that backs up the main idea that the library is helpful.
blocks.rule: A supporting detail is a smaller fact or example that backs up the main idea.

practiceItems.prompt: a fact that backs up the main idea is a ___ detail
the main idea is supported by several ___
details are ___ than the main idea (smaller/bigger)

blocks.content: Details often answer the questions who, what, when, where and why.

blocks.question: A supporting detail usually answers a question like:
options: what is the whole text about?
who, what, when, where or why?
blocks.explain: Details give specifics — who, what, when, where and why.
blocks.rule: Supporting details answer questions like who, what, when, where and why.

practiceItems.prompt: details often answer who, what, when, where and ___
a detail gives ___ about the main idea (specifics/nothing)
the main idea is backed up by supporting ___

blocks.question: The main idea is 'Exercise keeps you healthy.' Which sentence is a supporting detail?
options: 'It makes your heart stronger' — it gives a reason for the main idea
blocks.explain: Supporting details back up the main idea with reasons or examples. 'It makes your heart stronger' explains WHY exercise keeps you healthy, so it supports the main idea. The cat sentence has nothing to do with it.
blocks.rule: Supporting details give reasons or examples for the main idea.
blocks.principle: Details must connect to and strengthen the main idea.
canonical_solution: Main idea: exercise keeps you healthy
A detail gives a reason or example
'makes your heart stronger' is a reason
So it is the supporting detail

rubric.look_for: checks which sentence links to the main idea
picks the heart sentence as support
explains details back up the main idea

misconceptions.coach: A detail must connect to the main idea.
That gives no reason or example.

practiceItems.prompt: sentences that back up the main idea are supporting
should a detail relate to the main idea? (yes/no)
is an unrelated sentence a good detail? (yes/no)

blocks.content: Supporting details are the small facts that prove the main idea. Look for the who, what, when, where and why. Let's practise!
